question: I'm heading off on a two-month trip to Australia over Christmas and the house will be completely empty. Do I need to let you know beforehand, and what do I have to do with the heating or water so I'm still covered if a pipe bursts?
expected: Yes. Tell your broker if the home will be unoccupied for over 60 days. For escape of water while unoccupied, keep the heating at a minimum of 10C from November to March, or turn off and drain the water system
author: written independently of the glossary

question: My dog just chewed through the bottom of a brand-new leather sofa and scratched up the wooden door frame. Am I covered for pet damage under my buildings or contents, and is there a limit?
expected: Yes, damage by chewing, scratching, tearing, vomiting or fouling by pets is covered but limited to £5,000 under contents and £5,000 under buildings
author: written independently of the glossary

question: Someone smashed the window of my car while it was parked at the supermarket and stole my backpack from the back seat. Can I claim for my stolen stuff on my Basic home contents policy?
expected: No. Theft from vehicle is not covered on Basic (Silver and Gold only)
author: written independently of the glossary

question: I'm planning to renovate my kitchen next month, just ripping out the old units and fitting new ones without knocking down any walls. Do I have to tell you before the builders start?
expected: No. Replacing or refitting existing kitchen fittings with no structural changes does not need to be reported; other building work needs 30 days' notice
author: written independently of the glossary

question: My son is moving into university halls in September with his laptop and musical instruments. Are his things covered under my home contents policy while he's away at uni, and what if someone steals them from his room?
expected: Student belongings in halls or term-time accommodation are covered up to the amount in the schedule; theft is only covered if there is evidence of forcible and violent entry
author: written independently of the glossary

question: Last night's storm blew down two panels of my garden fence and knocked over my shed. Will my buildings insurance cover the cost of replacing the fence and fixing the shed?
expected: Storm damage to gates, hedges and fences is excluded, so not the fence. The shed is part of the buildings and is not excluded from storm cover
author: written independently of the glossary

question: I'm having a single-storey extension built next spring and the builder's quote is around £85,000 including VAT. Am I automatically covered during the work, or do I need to call you before they start?
expected: Building works over £75,000 including VAT must be notified and agreed before work starts, otherwise loss or damage is not covered
author: written independently of the glossary

question: I left my handbag in the unlocked footwell of my car while I nipped into the petrol station and someone grabbed it. Will my contents cover pay for my stolen purse and cash?
expected: No. Theft from an unattended motor vehicle is only covered if all windows were closed and doors locked (limit £15,000); personal money excludes theft from an unattended vehicle
author: written independently of the glossary

question: We had a massive water leak from an upstairs radiator that caused over £25,000 of damage. I saw something in the booklet about getting money towards a smart leak detector; how does that work?
expected: After an escape of water claim, Covea pays up to £2,500 including survey costs towards installing a water leak detection and prevention system
author: written independently of the glossary

question: I just bought a vintage watch at an auction for £12,000. Is it covered right away under my policy, and do I need to get an official valuation done?
expected: New purchases are covered if you tell them within 60 days and pay any extra premium; a single watch is limited to £10,000 unless specified; a valuation is needed for claims
author: written independently of the glossary

question: I accidentally left the bath tap running upstairs and water overflowed through the kitchen ceiling. Is the water damage to my ceiling and carpets covered under my Basic policy?
expected: No. Loss or damage caused by water overflowing because taps were left on in sinks or baths is excluded under both buildings and contents
author: written independently of the glossary

question: My e-bike was locked to a bike rack outside the train station and someone cut the lock and stole it. Can I claim for it on my Basic home insurance?
expected: E-bikes up to 250 watts count as pedal cycles; theft away from home is only covered under personal possessions (if shown on the schedule) and only if locked to an immovable object
author: written independently of the glossary

question: We had a power cut yesterday and everything in our chest freezer defrosted and had to be binned. Can I claim back the cost of the ruined food?
expected: No. Freezer contents are not covered on Basic (Bronze £400, Silver £500, Gold £750)
author: written independently of the glossary

question: A really heavy rainstorm flooded our back garden and seeped under the patio doors, ruining the wooden floor in the lounge. Does that count as a flood, and what if the water just came up through the ground?
expected: Storm or flood damage is covered, but damage as a result of a rise in the water table is excluded
author: written independently of the glossary

question: I'm renting a flat and accidentally dropped a heavy pan on the landlord's ceramic hob and cracked it. Does my contents policy cover me for damage I cause to the landlord's fixtures?
expected: Tenant's liability covers landlord's fixtures only for the listed causes such as fire or theft; accidental breakage needs the optional accidental damage cover
author: written independently of the glossary

question: I've got a really nasty boundary dispute going on with my next-door neighbour who just built a wall onto my driveway. If I have your optional Family Legal Expenses cover, will you pay for a solicitor?
expected: Property infringement covers legal action for nuisance or trespass, subject to a 180 day waiting period and at least a 51% chance of success
author: written independently of the glossary
